I can do this, but because this will remove or move files (destructive/irreversible), I need one confirmation first.

Planned action (recommended — non‑destructive):
- Create a folder Employee handbook/Archive - old drafts.
- Move documents in the Employee handbook folder that I judge to be stale drafts into that Archive folder. I will consider a document a stale draft if it meets one or more of these heuristics:
  - Title contains draft indicators (e.g., "draft", "DRAFT", "v0", "v1", "copy", "old"), or
  - Last modified more than ~12 months ago and there is a more recent live version present, or
  - Document content contains a visible "DRAFT" header or similar language.
- Keep the live/current handbook in place (I will avoid moving the most recent non‑draft file).
- I will not delete anything permanently unless you explicitly ask for deletion.

Alternative (destructive):
- Permanently delete the files matching the same heuristics above (irreversible).

Please confirm one of these choices:
1) "Archive — proceed" — move staged stale drafts to Employee handbook/Archive - old drafts (recommended).
2) "Delete — proceed" — permanently delete stale drafts.
3) "Cancel" — do nothing.

Reply with exactly one of those three options and I will proceed.
